---
title: AI assistants
description: "Set up an assistant in Positron, let it read the course rules, and work with it so that you can defend every line."
---

You may, and you are expected to, use AI assistants for code, text and review. In exchange, the bar is high: you answer for every line you hand in. The [assignment quality criteria](assignment-quality-criteria.qmd) say what that means in detail. This page covers the practical side: setting up an assistant, the course rules it reads, and a way of working that holds up.

## Set up an assistant in Positron

Positron Assistant gives you a chat (to ask, to edit files, or as an agent that works across the project) and code completion while you type.

1. **A model provider.** GitHub Copilot is free for students with the [GitHub Student Developer Pack](https://education.github.com/pack). Alternatively, use an API key from Anthropic, which you pay per use.
2. **Turn it on.** In Positron's settings, search for *Positron Assistant: Enable* and tick it. Then reload the window: *Ctrl+Shift+P* (*Cmd+Shift+P* on a Mac), *Developer: Reload Window*.
3. **Sign in.** *Ctrl+Shift+P*, *Positron Assistant: Configure Language Model Providers*, choose your provider and sign in.

The [Positron documentation](https://positron.posit.co/assistant) shows every step with screenshots. Other assistants, such as Claude Code or Copilot in VS Code, work in the same project and read the same rules.

## The course rules your assistant reads

The course repository, and your team's copy of it, contains a file `AGENTS.md`. It tells assistants how this course works, in short:

- packages only through uvr and uv, and how to render;
- tidyverse with `|>` in R, polars in Python, code no more complex than the task;
- licensed data read by code, never shown in the chat;
- numbers in the text from inline code, labelled figures and tables, only references that exist.

Positron Assistant, Copilot and Claude Code read it automatically when you open the repository folder, so you don't have to repeat these rules in every chat. Don't edit `AGENTS.md`: course updates change it. Put your team's own rules into `.github/instructions/team.instructions.md`, which Positron and Copilot also read:

```markdown
---
applyTo: "**"
---
We write all code in Python. Figures use plotnine with theme_minimal().
```

## A way of working that holds up

1. **Ask before you build.** Describe the question, the data and the method, and ask for a plan before any code. Disagree with the plan where you know better.
2. **One step at a time.** Let the assistant change one chunk or one function, run it, and look at the result before the next step.
3. **Check the numbers yourself.** Compare with a value you know (from the lecture, the book chapter or a second, simpler computation) and with common sense: a monthly return of 40 % or a Sharpe ratio of 5 is a bug until proven otherwise.
4. **Read the changes before you commit.** The *Source Control* panel shows every changed line. If you cannot explain a line, rewrite or delete it.
5. **Render the whole report** after each round of changes, so the text, tables and figures still agree.
6. **Let AI review the result** with the [review prompt in the quality criteria](assignment-quality-criteria.qmd#let-ai-review-your-submission), then decide yourself what to change.

## Licensed data and tokens

- **Never paste rows of CRSP or other licensed data into a chat, and never upload the files.** An assistant in agent mode can read the files in your project; `AGENTS.md` tells it to look at licensed data only through column names, types and summaries. Check that it does.
- **Never paste your trading game token** into a chat. It belongs in `.Renviron` or `.env`, where `set_token()` puts it.
- Check your provider's privacy settings: some providers store your prompts or use them for training.
